final_answer: UniLectin fungal lectin data for Aspergillus niger (limited to 1000 entries) reveals a diverse repertoire of structural folds and domains. Distinct fold–domain combinations observed include: (1) a/b barrel (TIM) fold – chi-lectin (TCLL); (2) b-sandwich / cyanovirin-like – cyanovirin-like; (3) b-prism I – Jacalin-like; (4) small protein / Knottin – hevein-like and Lyophyllum ginkbilobin-like; (5) b-sandwich / cytolysin-like – Fungal fruit body lectin and Oomycete cytolysin; (6) a/b mixed / LysM domain – LysM-like; (7) b-barrel – P-type lectin-like; (8) b-sandwich / ConA-like – ERGIC-VIP L-type and Yeast Emp L-type; (9) b-trefoil – Ricin-like and Laetiporus trefoil lectin-like; (10) b-sandwich / Galactose-binding domain-like – H-type lectin; and (11) ab hairpin, non-globular proline-rich – calnexin-calreticulin-like. Comparison shows the b-sandwich fold is the most prevalent (spanning ConA-like, cyanovirin-like, cytolysin-like, and galactose-binding subtypes), while a/b mixed LysM-like and Knottin/hevein-like entries are also highly recurrent, indicating both β-sheet-rich and small disulfide-stabilized lectin architectures coexist in this species.
